lead.headline: CABINET CLEARS REWORKED WOMEN’S QUOTA AND DELIMITATION BILLS
lead.deck: The proposals link 33% reservation to a 50% expansion of seats in every state; Parliament must still approve the bills.
paragraphs: The Union Cabinet has approved revised bills to implement one-third reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies through delimitation. The package proposes increasing the number of seats by 50% in every state and Union Territory.

The draft would use the 2011 Census to redraw constituencies while freezing the existing inter-state share of seats through 2051. The Lok Sabha is scheduled to reconvene on November 30 and the Rajya Sabha on December 2; these are proposals awaiting Parliament’s approval, not enacted changes.

image.alt: Union Cabinet meeting, accompanying a report on the proposed women's reservation and delimitation bills.
image.caption: The Cabinet cleared the revised bills on Friday; Parliament will decide whether they become law. Photo: The Indian Express.

sidebarStory.headline: ₹2,321-CRORE WHITE-TOPPING PLAN COVERS 88 BENGALURU ROADS
sidebarStory.subhead: The project spans five city corporations, with tenders expected within three months.
paragraphs: Karnataka has approved white-topping for 88 roads across Bengaluru’s five city corporations under a ₹2,321-crore project. Cubbon Road, Langford Road, Victoria Road and Old Airport Road are among the named stretches.
Plans include continuous footpaths, crossings and junction upgrades, along with utility work intended to reduce repeat digging. The detailed project reports and tendering process are still to come.

image.alt: Representational AI-generated illustration for Bengaluru's proposed white-topping road project.
image.caption: A representational visual accompanying the project report. Image: The Times of India.

stories.headline: KARNATAKA BARS THREE IOCL TERMINAL METERS OVER READING DISCREPANCIES
paragraphs: The state’s legal metrology department has taken three mass-flow meters at an Indian Oil Corporation terminal in Devanagonthi out of commercial use after finding discrepancies in recorded petrol and ethanol measurements.
Officials issued a show-cause notice and are investigating. The action concerns terminal measurement equipment; it does not establish adulteration or short delivery at retail pumps.

stories.headline: PHOTO CHECKS FLAG LOW HELPER ATTENDANCE ON GARBAGE ROUTES
paragraphs: Bengaluru Solid Waste Management Ltd’s photo-based attendance checks have found that only around 10–20% of assigned garbage-collection helpers were appearing for duty at some mustering points, a report says.

The system records vehicles, drivers and helpers as trucks enter and leave. The early findings are being used to examine attendance and payments; the city’s waste collection service remains in operation.

stories.headline: FISH KILL REPORTED AT JAKKUR LAKE; WATER TESTS UNDER WAY
paragraphs: Dead fish were reported at north Bengaluru’s Jakkur Lake on Friday. Civic officials collected water samples after a possible sewage-pipeline leak was raised as one cause.
Results are expected in several days. Lake volunteers also said seasonal changes and low dissolved oxygen can contribute to fish deaths, so the cause has not yet been confirmed.

stories.headline: SC ORDERS DEEPATHOON LAMP LIGHTING TODAY; CRPF TO SECURE HILL
paragraphs: The Supreme Court directed that the ceremonial lamp be lit at the Deepathoon on Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai on November 28, with devotees allowed to participate at a distance of at least 50 metres from the dargah.

The court ordered CRPF security for the temple and dargah, suspended the temple trustees and appointed former judges as receivers. It also issued contempt notices over alleged non-compliance with its earlier order; the wider dispute remains before the court.

stories.headline: ALLAHABAD HC QUASHES UPPSC PCS PRELIMS RESULT, ORDERS FRESH MAINS
paragraphs: The Allahabad High Court quashed the UPPSC PCS-2025 preliminary results and directed the commission to redraw the merit list under reservation rules before holding the Mains examination afresh.

More than 626,000 candidates applied for the preliminary test for 814 posts. The ruling followed a challenge over meritorious reserved-category candidates not being moved to the unreserved list when their marks exceeded its cut-off.

stories.headline: ATS ARRESTS MAN SUSPECTED OF JE M LINKS; AK-47 SEIZED IN VADODARA
paragraphs: Gujarat’s Anti-Terrorism Squad arrested a man in Vadodara on suspicion of links to Pakistan-based Jaish-e-Mohammed, seizing an AK-47 and 23 rounds of ammunition, the agency said.
Investigators allege he had surveyed sensitive sites and was in contact with a handler. The case is under investigation and the allegations have not been tested in court.

image.alt: Photograph published with a report on a suspect arrested by Gujarat ATS in Vadodara.
image.caption: Gujarat ATS said it seized an AK-47 and ammunition. Photo: India Today.

groups.ariaLabel: India economy, infrastructure and public policy news

stories.headline: RUPEE STRENGTHENS AS RBI LETS FOREIGN INFLOWS TEST THE RALLY
paragraphs: The rupee has strengthened as foreign investors returned to Indian equities, with Reuters reporting that the Reserve Bank of India has allowed the currency to rise rather than immediately buying dollars to rebuild reserves.
The shift follows heavy RBI intervention when the rupee approached a record low earlier this year. Currency moves remain sensitive to oil prices, global yields and capital flows.

stories.headline: 6.59-KM TUNNEL BREAKTHROUGH ADVANCES RISHIKESH–KARNAPRAYAG RAIL LINK
paragraphs: Railways reported a breakthrough connecting the two excavated sections of Tunnel-14, a 6.59-km tunnel in Rudraprayag district on the Rishikesh–Karnaprayag project.

Engineers used staged excavation through loose soil beneath inhabited areas. The project is intended to improve rail access to Uttarakhand’s hill districts; the breakthrough is a construction milestone, not the opening of the line.

stories.headline: TAMIL NADU ADDS 15 DAYS OF PATERNITY LEAVE FOR STATE EMPLOYEES
paragraphs: Male Tamil Nadu government employees will be eligible for 15 days of paternity leave, which can be taken shortly before an expected delivery or within six months after a child’s birth.
The state announced the provision as a new benefit for its workforce. It broadens leave options for new fathers; the report does not describe it as a policy for all private-sector workers.

stories.headline: INDIA TAKE THREE WICKETS, BUT NZ REACH 330/8 AT DAY 2 LUNCH
paragraphs: New Zealand moved from 246/5 overnight to 330/8 by lunch on Day 2 of the second Test in Christchurch. Tom Blundell was unbeaten on 80 as India’s bowlers took three wickets in the morning session.
Akash Deep had 4/84 at the interval. This is a live match update: New Zealand were still batting, with two wickets left, when the report was filed.

image.alt: India fast bowler Akash Deep during the second Test against New Zealand in Christchurch.
image.caption: Akash Deep took four wickets by lunch on Day 2. Photo: AP / India Today.

stories.headline: INDIA SET UP FINAL AGAINST CHINA AFTER 6–2 WIN OVER MALAYSIA
paragraphs: Defending champions India beat Malaysia 6–2 in the semi-final of the Women’s Asian Champions Trophy in Bhopal, booking a place in the final against China on Saturday.
The result sends India into the title match for a sixth time. The tournament is being held at the International Sports Complex in Nathu Barkheda.

stories.headline: IOA PRESENTS INDIA’S 2036 OLYMPIC ROADMAP TO IOC COMMISSION
paragraphs: The Indian Olympic Association presented its proposed vision and roadmap for the 2036 Olympic and Paralympic Games to the International Olympic Committee’s Future Host Commission.
The virtual presentation highlighted Ahmedabad’s proposed venue clusters and infrastructure plans. It is part of the IOC’s host-selection dialogue; India has not been awarded the Games.
